model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the “effect” (y-axis, ranging from 0 to 30 with major ticks at intervals of 10) of six different language models — mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂ — across nine language families or groups (x-axis: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, Uralic). Each group on the x-axis contains six vertically aligned bars, color-coded according to the legend in the upper right: light blue for mBERT-L₂, dark blue for XLM-L₂, light green for mBERT-R₂, dark green for XLM-R₂, light pink for mBERT-B₂, and red for XLM-B₂. Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating variability or confidence intervals. The chart shows substantial variation in effect size across both models and language groups; for example, in the IE-Indic group, all models show relatively high effects (ranging roughly from 15 to 25), whereas in the Isolate and Uralic groups, most models show near-zero effects. The IE-Slavic family and Semitic groups also exhibit high effects for several models, particularly XLM-B₂ and mBERT-B₂. Bars are not sorted by height within groups, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding and error bars. The overall pattern suggests that model performance (as measured by “effect”) varies significantly depending on the linguistic family being evaluated.
